name: precondition-fork-approved
description:
The APPROVED half of the fork gate: same fixture as precondition-fork-gated, but the waiver is auto-APPROVED, and the checkout is called TWICE to prove the grant the waiver writes PERSISTS. A pull_request webhook opens the session; its head is on a fork, so the github kind records envelope fact head_is_fork=true keyed to the head OID. The FIRST checkout of that OID is Refused by the git_commit slot's `requires: [!facts.envelope.head_is_fork]` and raises a precondition_waiver card (recorded decision: denied). A human with session-approve standing approves it; BindApproved(PreconditionsWaived) writes the slot grant for that commit and the call proceeds. The SECOND checkout of the same OID finds the persisted grant and records `allowed` — no second card.

Why TWO calls. The waiver path proceeds-on-approved rather than re-dispatching (Task 5), so the first call records only its pre-card `denied`; the `allowed` decision is produced by a later call that finds the bound grant — the same durability shape plangate-external-covered-by-approved-slot uses to prove a grant persists rather than being consumed once. The final outcome on git_commit:<head OID>#checkout is `allowed`, reachable ONLY through the waiver: the slot starts empty (fillFrom is observed and nothing observed this commit) and the precondition is Refused, so nothing but a human's consent can produce it. The decision transition across the pair — denied in the gated twin, [denied, allowed] here — is what proves the card is real, not just that a call was refused. It is read from the decision log, not the tool result, because bronze runs no ToolCall controller: an allowed sandbox call STILL returns an error (nothing executes), exactly as git-repo-url-allows-granted notes: each checkout step asserts only that its last tool result was the checkout call, and the `allowed` final decision carries the whole claim.

The auto-approver clicks as the harness DefaultUser, who is the session owner (Channel.owner.explicit) and so holds approve on the session; the precondition declares no approvers of its own, so the waiver routes to the slot's session-only standing and the click folds to CheckApprove(agentsession#approve). The fixture is self-contained: its own AgentClass and a fixture SpiceboxToolkit (forkgit) declaring git_commit; toolkits/git.yaml is untouched.

args._reason: check out the pull request head to read its code
re-check out the same head commit; the waiver already cleared it

reply.text: The fork checkout was approved and the grant persisted; I reviewed the head commit.
